full_judgment:
Md Abdur Razzaque J: This Rule under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure (Act V of 1908) at the instance of the defendants-petitioners is directed against the order No. 33 dated 9-10-95 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 1st Additional Court, Gaibandha Sadar, in Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1994 allowing restoration of the original suit to its file and number upon setting aside the impugned order dated 4-10- 95. 

 3. The plaintiff-opposite party filed the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1994 under Order IX rule 9 of the Code for restoration of the suit after setting aside the said dismissal order dated 23-1-94. The defendant-petitioner resisted the said Miscellaneous Case by filing a written objection. The learned Assistant Judge, 1st Additional Court by his order No. 30 dated 19-8-95 allowed the said Miscellaneous Case, awarding a cost of Taka 1,000 to be paid to the defendant-petitioners within 45 days from the date of the order, Thereafter, in view of filing an application by the plaintiff for exempting her from paying the cost, the learned Assistant Judge reduced the cost from Taka 1,000 to Taka 700 directing the plaintiff to deposit the cost within the stipulated time by his order dated 19-9- 95. Thereafter, as the cost was not deposited within time given by the Court, so, the order No. 30 by which the Miscellaneous Case No.1 of 1994 was allowed earlier is held against the plaintiff opposite party by order No. 32 dated 4-10-95. Subsequently, in view of an application filed by the plaintiff opposite party praying to restore the original suit allowing the Miscellaneous case on acceptance of the cost deposited by cheques on 7-10-95, the learned Assistant Judge upon hearing restored the original Suit to its file and number upon setting aside the order dated 4-10-95 vide his order No. 33 dated 9-10-95. 

 5. Mr Akram Hossain Amin, the learned Senior Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submits that the learned Assistant Judge committed clear illegality in restoring the Original Suit on acceptance of the cost not deposited within the given time on 4-10-95. He further submits that the order dated 4-10-95 impliedly dismissing the Miscellaneous Case for non-payment of costs being an appellate order under Order XLIII and rule 1 (c) of the Code, the learned Assistant Judge erred in law in passing the impugned order dated 9-10-95, resulting in failure of justice. 

 9. Admittedly, the original Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1994 was allowed subject to the payment of cost of Taka 1,000 within 45 days. It is also admitted that on an application filed by the plaintiff-opposite party on 19-9-95 the cost was reduced to Taka 700 with a direction to deposit the same within the time fixed. It is also admitted that for failure of taking steps by the plaintiff opposite party regarding deposit of cost on 4-10-95, the conditional order of restoration of the original suit allowing the Miscellaneous Case No.1 of 1994 dated 19-8-95 was held against the plaintiffs- opposite party. Order No. 33 dated 9-10-95 indicates that in view of the prayer made by the plaintiff-(opposite party) supported by affidavit and deposit of cost of Taka 700 by two cheques, on 7-10-95 the learned trial Court upon hearing the plaintiffs opposite parties allowed the same and thereby restored the original suit to its file and number upon setting aside the dismissal order dated 4-10-95. 

 10. It is true that if an application under Order IX rule 9 of the Code is dismissed for default, then this becomes an appealable order under Order XLIII rule 1(c) but the question is when the case is not for default but for non-payment of cost. Then can it be set aside invoking section 151 of the Code on acceptance of the costs subsequently. On this question, I may refer to the case of Rafiqul Islam and other vs Abul Kalam and others, reported in 42 DLR 19. In that case, it has been observed: 

 "In this case from the facts it appears that the application under section 151 of the Code was filed for restoration of the suit on setting aside the order of dismissal of the Miscellaneous Case which was dismissed not for appearance of the plaintiff when the case was taken up for hearing but for not depositing the cost within time allowed by the court. The power under section 151 of the Code is not a new one, it is inherent by virtue of its duty to do justice between the parties before it and it is within the province of the court to invoke such power to secure the ends of justice regard being had to the facts and circumstances of a given case." 

 11. In the instant case the order of dismissal of the Original suit dated 23-1-94 was set aside in Miscellaneous Case No.1 of 1994 on 19-9-95 subjecting the same to the payment of costs of Taka 1000 to the defendant opposite party within 45 days. This period fixed by the order could be enlarged under Section 148 of the Code, which reads as follows: 

 13. For the reason as above, it may be held that no appeal under Order XLIII, rule 1 (c) of the Code lies against an order terminating the dismissal order for non-payment of costs in a case under Order IX rule 9 of the Code, in allowing the restoration of the original suit (restored earlier), the conditional cost being paid and accepted by the court subsequently. 

 14. Be that as it may, from the impugned order dated 9-10-95 it indicates that in consideration of the reasons assigned in the application of the miscellaneous case learned Assistant Judge, on being satisfied, exercised his power in allowing the prayer for acceptance of the deposit and set aside the impugned order dated 4-10-95 and thereby restored the original suit to its original file and number. In the facts and circumstances of the instant case, the learned Assistant Judge, appears to have committed no illegality in passing the impugned order to ensure single-handed justice relieving the parties from further litigation’s in other forums and accordingly I find noting to interfere with the impugned order. 

 16. The impugned order dated 9-10-95 passed by the learned Assistant Judge in Miscellaneous Case No.1 of 1994 is affirmed.
